dossiers.title: Curse of the Dead Gods
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Combat requires managing stamina for dodges and attacks, parrying enemy blows and choosing weapons with different timings, ranges and effects.
Corruption rises through blood bargains, entering rooms and enemy hits, adding curses that can help or hinder until dangerously high levels change a run.
Shorter routes build toward longer temples and final mixed dungeons; branching room rewards, hazards and boss encounters give each run tactical decisions.
Persistent upgrades open new weapons, blessings and options, while the player's grasp of timing often matters more than permanent statistics.
Players describe tough but learnable enemies and bosses and deliberate stamina pacing; hard final temples can push difficulty beyond what some consider fun.
Late replay value is contested: weapon and relic combinations invite mastery, yet repeated rooms and inflated boss durability can make longer endgame runs feel tedious.
The hand-drawn look and oppressive temple lighting create tension, with darkness changing both visibility and the risks of traps or enemies.
Story and character writing are minimal, mostly relegated to bestiary entries, which suits a systems-first action game but disappoints players seeking Hades-like narrative motivation.
Some players consider curse combinations overly restrictive and later boss runs too long; others value managing those tradeoffs as the game's central skill.

dossiers.title: Sherlock Holmes Chapter One
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Investigations combine finding evidence, disguises, eavesdropping, re-enacting events and connecting propositions in the mind palace, with room for several interpretations of a case.
A Mediterranean open island offers main mysteries and side cases that players may discover by overhearing conversations or visiting districts, though investigations remain authored.
A young Sherlock and his childhood companion Jon create an emotionally charged story about his mother's death, praised by some and rejected by others as out of character.
Clue matching, pinning journal notes and finding specific witnesses can feel like guessing rather than logical deduction, and players dislike uncertain post-case verdicts.
The optional-looking combat arenas receive recurrent complaints for repetitive stun-and-arrest shooting and clumsy controls that clash with detective play.
Although Cordona's districts look attractive, travel between dispersed clues and comparatively few interactive interiors can make the open world seem empty or stretched out.
Progress depends more on completing cases and unlocking story context than on building character statistics; clothing and disguise options sometimes gate access to witnesses.
The case variety and emotional investigations can sustain long play sessions, but repeated deductions, navigation and action arenas wear thin for others.
Player reports include city traversal slowdown and occasional quest progression issues in 2022; current frequency cannot be established from the dated reviews.

dossiers.title: Monster Prom 2: Monster Camp
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The camp-themed dating sim uses choice-based dialogue, stat-driven interactions and event outcomes to pursue monster characters over short repeatable playthroughs.
Absurd, self-aware jokes, eccentric monsters and vibrant art are the main recurring attraction; the tone is deliberately exaggerated rather than realistic romance.
Local or online sessions can become a playful group activity with shared jokes, but one player regards it as parallel turn-taking with little actual interaction.
Numerous events, routes, unlockable endings and changing partners motivate several repeated short runs, while the core choice structure stays similar.
A run is largely text and dialogue choices; players seeking interactive systems may find the reading-heavy, turn-based pace slow or passive.
Players praise distinctive music, character writing and optional romantic outcomes, although some want more depth or prefer other characters in the roster.
Success depends on interpreting personalities and choices, and some players find hidden conditions for regular or secret endings unintuitive.
One player feels that story and numerical outcome systems lose meaning when played alone; another dislikes the limited direct interaction between multiplayer turns.
A Russian-speaking 2022 reviewer asked for Russian translation and official Steam metadata still lists only English subtitles and interface; text-heavy writing may be a substantial language barrier.
